summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish task forces to develop technical standards for identifying and labeling content created or modified by generative artificial intelligence. It also requires creators of generative AI applications and large online platforms to include and display machine-readable disclosures or metadata on AI-generated audio and visual content, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.

affected_groups.effect: Must incorporate machine-readable AI origin disclosures and tamper-resistant metadata into generated or modified audio and visual content, and prevent the removal of these disclosures.

Websites and applications with at least $50,000,000 in annual revenue or 25,000,000 monthly active users must clearly and conspicuously display AI content disclosures to users and are prohibited from removing disclosures or metadata.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology must establish and manage multiple task forces and submit reports to Congress, while the Federal Trade Commission must issue regulations and enforce compliance.

key_provisions: Requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish task forces within 90 days to support technical standards for content provenance, watermarking, and digital fingerprinting for audio, visual, and text-based AI content.

Mandates that providers of generative AI applications incorporate machine-readable disclosures into created or modified audio or visual content that acknowledge its AI origin and prevent tampering with these disclosures.
Requires AI software applications to provide users with metadata containing tamper-evident details such as the application name, model version, creation date and time, and modified portions.
Prohibits covered online platforms from removing disclosures or metadata on audio or visual content and requires them to clearly and conspicuously show the disclosure information to users.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to promulgate regulations within 2 years, enforce the requirements as unfair or deceptive acts or practices, and establish safe harbors for approved self-regulatory guidelines.
missing_information: Specific financial penalty amounts for violating the FTC enforcement rules.
The exact composition or number of members for the NIST task forces beyond general categories.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act requires the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to establish task forces to develop technical standards for identifying and labeling content created or modified by generative artificial intelligence. It also requires creators of generative AI applications and large online platforms to include and display machine-readable disclosures or metadata on AI-generated audio and visual content, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.
summary_detail.significance: This bill sets up formal federal processes to standardize AI content identification and creates mandatory labeling and disclosure rules for large online platforms and AI developers, backed by Federal Trade Commission enforcement.
